Hydra Vertex Documentation

3D models, vertex shaders, and geometry in Hydra

What is a Vertex Shader?

Standard Hydra uses fragment shaders - programs that run once per pixel to determine its color. Every pixel is processed independently, which is why Hydra patterns tile across the entire screen.

Vertex shaders run once per vertex (corner point) of geometry. They transform 3D positions into 2D screen coordinates and pass data like normals and texture coordinates to the fragment shader.

// Traditional Hydra (fragment shader only) // Runs for every pixel, no 3D geometry osc(10).out(o0) // Hydra Vertex (vertex + fragment shader) // Vertex shader transforms 3D model // Fragment shader colors each pixel of the model osc(10).out(o0, model.perspective(45))

With vertex shaders, Hydra can:

  • Render 3D models with perspective
  • Access vertex attributes (position, normal, UV) in your code
  • Apply Hydra textures to geometry surfaces
  • Animate skeletal meshes

Loading 3D Models

Hydra Vertex adds support for loading and rendering 3D models. Models are loaded asynchronously and can be used as geometry for Hydra textures.

loadGlb(url)

Loads a GLB/GLTF model. Supports skeletal animation.

// Load a GLB model loadGlb('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/AnimalKit/Cat.glb') .then(model => { osc(10).color(1, 0.5, 0.2) .out(o0, model.rotateX(3.14).rotateY(() => time).perspective(45)) })

loadObj(url)

Loads an OBJ model. Good for static geometry.

// Load an OBJ model loadObj('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/AnimalKit/Alpaca.obj') .then(model => { gradient(0.5).out(o0, model.rotateY(() => time * 0.5).perspective(45)) })

Model Transforms

Once loaded, models can be transformed using chainable methods:

Method Description
.rotateX(angle) Rotate around X axis (radians or function)
.rotateY(angle) Rotate around Y axis
.rotateZ(angle) Rotate around Z axis
.scale(s) Uniform scale
.translate(x, y, z) Move in 3D space
.perspective(fov) Apply perspective projection (field of view in degrees)
// Combining transforms loadGlb('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/AnimalKit/Fox.glb') .then(model => { noise(3, 0.2).color(1, 0.6, 0.2) .out(o0, model .rotateX(3.14) .rotateY(() => time) .scale(1.5) .translate(0, -0.2, 0) .perspective(60)) })

Skeletal Animation

GLB models with skeletal animations can be animated using the .animate() method.

// Animated character loadGlb('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/AnimatedWomenPack/Breakdance.glb') .then(model => { osc(5, 0.1).color(0.8, 0.2, 0.6) .out(o0, model.animate().rotateX(3.14).scale(0.8).perspective(45)) })

Animation Options

Method Description
.animate() Play the default animation
.animate('name') Play animation by name
.animate('name', () => time) Control animation time with a function

Sprite Levels

The .out() function accepts an optional third parameter for sprite level rendering. This allows layering multiple geometries or rendering modes on the same output.

Syntax

texture().out(output, geometry, level)
Parameter Description
output Output buffer (o0, o1, o2, o3)
geometry Optional geometry/model to render onto
level Sprite level (0 = background, 1+ = foreground layers)

Level 0 (Default)

Standard full-screen rendering. This is the default when no level is specified.

// Default rendering (level 0) osc(10).out(o0)

Level 1+ (Sprite Layers)

Higher levels render as sprites on top of lower levels. Use this to composite 3D geometry over a background.

// Background layer (level 0) osc(5, 0.1).color(0.2, 0.1, 0.3).out(o0) // Load model on sprite level 1 (foreground) loadGlb('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/AnimalKit/Dog.glb') .then(model => { solid(1, 0.8, 0.5) .out(o0, model.rotateX(3.14).rotateY(() => time).perspective(45), 1) })
Tip: Sprite levels allow you to create complex compositions with multiple 3D objects, each with their own textures, layered over animated backgrounds.

Vertex Attributes

When rendering with geometry, you can access vertex attributes using the v proxy:

Attribute Description
v.position Vertex position (vec3)
v.normal Vertex normal (vec3)
v.uv Texture coordinates (vec2)
// Color by vertex normals loadGlb('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/AnimalKit/Bear.glb') .then(model => { solid(v.normal.x, v.normal.y, v.normal.z) .out(o0, model.rotateX(3.14).rotateY(() => time).perspective(45)) })
Note: Vertex attributes like v.normal only contain meaningful data when geometry is passed to .out(). Without geometry, they default to zero.

Sprite Sheets

Sprite sheets are textures containing multiple frames of animation arranged in a grid. Hydra Vertex can load sprite sheets and animate through the frames.

Loading a Sprite Sheet

Use loadSprite() to load a sprite sheet image and specify the grid dimensions.

loadSprite(url, columns, rows)
Parameter Description
url URL to the sprite sheet image
columns Number of columns in the grid
rows Number of rows in the grid

Sprite Methods

Method Description
.frame(n) Display a specific frame (0-indexed)
.frame(() => expr) Animate frames with a function
.scale(s) Scale the sprite
.translate(x, y) Position the sprite

Animating Through Frames

Use a time-based function to cycle through frames:

// Animate through a 4x4 sprite sheet loadSprite('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/test-grid-4x4.png', 4, 4) .then(sprite => { src(sprite.frame(() => Math.floor(time * 8) % 16)) .out(o0) })

Combining Sprites with Effects

Sprites work with all standard Hydra functions:

// Sprite with oscillator blend on level 1 loadSprite('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/test-grid-4x4.png', 4, 4) .then(sprite => { osc(10, 0.1).color(0.5, 0.2, 0.8).out(o0) src(sprite.frame(() => Math.floor(time * 8) % 16).scale(0.5)) .mult(osc(20)) .out(o0, null, 1) })
Note: The frame index wraps around automatically. Use modulo (%) with the total frame count to loop through all frames.

Creative Examples

Oscillating Texture on Model

// Modulated oscillator on a rabbit loadGlb('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/AnimalKit/Rabbit.glb') .then(model => { osc(20, 0.1, 1.5) .modulate(noise(3), 0.1) .color(1, 0.8, 0.9) .out(o0, model.rotateX(3.14).rotateY(() => time * 0.3).perspective(50)) })

Feedback with 3D

// Feedback loop with geometry loadGlb('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/AnimalKit/Penguin.glb') .then(model => { src(o0).scale(1.01).rotate(0.01).blend(osc(10).color(0.2, 0.5, 1), 0.1) .out(o0, model.rotateX(3.14).rotateY(() => time * 0.5).perspective(45)) })

Dancing Character

// Dancing with hue shift loadGlb('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiefaye/hydra-models/main/AnimatedWomenPack/Rumba.glb') .then(model => { gradient(0.3).hue(() => time * 0.1) .out(o0, model.animate().rotateX(3.14).scale(0.7).perspective(45)) })

Available Models

Free models are available in the hydra-models repository:

AnimalKit (Static GLB)

Low-poly animals: Cat, Dog, Fox, Bear, Rabbit, Penguin, Deer, Horse, Cow, Shark, Frog, and more.

AnimatedWomenPack (Animated GLB)

Character animations: Breakdance, Rumba, Walking, and more.
